title: Resumable stream segment metadata harmonization and idempotent resume handshake
creator: Connor Lee
description: We need a robust, backwards-compatible resume handshake and compact per-segment metadata envelope so clients and servers can resume streaming responses with deterministic idempotency. Current reconnect behavior relies on coarse resume tokens that sometimes cause duplicate tool/function calls or truncated JSON in structured outputs. This ticket harmonizes a compact segment metadata schema (v1) and implements an idempotent resume handshake that servers can verify without heavy state, plus a graceful shim for legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: Define a 4-field segment metadata schema that fits into existing SSE comment fields and is interoperable with legacy clients
Implement a server-side resume handshake that allows stateless verification of resumed offsets (no per-client in-memory retention required)
Ensure resumed sessions are idempotent for function/tool calls: no duplicated function call deliveries to downstream tool runners
Provide a compatibility shim: server accepts both legacy resume tokens and new segment metadata, and logs mismatches for 30 days
Unit, integration, and canary e2e tests demonstrating resume across: short-lived mobile clients, long-poll proxies, and Dedicated pools
design_notes: Metadata schema v1: {stream_id, seg_seq, byte_offset, hash_prefix(8)} serialized as base64 JSON and placed in SSE comment `:md <payload>`

Resume handshake: client includes last-seen metadata in `Resume-Token` header on reconnect; server validates by re-hashing the referred fragment (hash_prefix) or consulting a short-lived segment index cache

Idempotency guarantee: tool/function call frames include an idempotency-stamp derived from stream_id+seg_seq+frame_seq; server will suppress duplicate emissions to tool runner if stamp seen within retention window

Stateless server mode: when segment index cache is empty, server will reject ambiguous resume attempts with 409 + body describing required minimal token (server asks client to restart from last full segment). This keeps server resource usage bounded
Compatibility shim: header `X-Redwood-Stream-Version` negotiates schema; server accepts legacy numeric token under `Resume-Offset` and maps it to nearest segment metadata where possible

Trade-offs: keeping a short-lived segment index cache per model shard (~2-5MB per shard) improves resume success rate but increases memory. We default to cache=false for low-tier Dedicated nodes; fallback to 409 responses

Security: hash_prefix is intentionally short (8 hex chars) to avoid leaking payload while enabling quick mismatch detection. Full segment hashes are only stored in ephemeral stores behind KMS-protected keys
implementation_notes: Server: add SegmentMetadataCodec in runtime/streaming (serialize/deserialize + validation); introduced config `stream.resume.cache_size`
Runtime: extend stream handshake to parse `Resume-Token` header and set resume_mode in request context
Tooling: add idempotency-stamp to function-call frames in the stream encoder; update tool-runner to dedupe on stamp (Redis-maintained TTL 5m)
Backward compatibility: implement token mapper that translates legacy `Resume-Offset` to metadata when offset maps to a segment boundary in the index; otherwise return 409 with guidance
Benchmark: local microbench shows resume validation adds ~0.6ms median to reconnect path when cache hit, ~3.4ms when hashing on-the-fly
Feature toggle: `enable_resumable_metadata_v1` default=true for hosted API; false for low-memory dedicated SKU until rollout completes
testing_plan: Unit tests: Codec roundtrip + invalid metadata fuzzing
Integration: simulate reconnects for 3 client types (JS SDK w/ SSE, mobile client over flaky LTE, proxy with buffering) and assert structured JSON outputs are complete post-resume
Property tests: idempotency-stamp uniqueness and dedupe behavior under concurrent reconnects
E2E canary: route 1% of traffic to runtime-2.0 with feature toggle on; monitor duplicate tool calls and structured output truncations
Chaos: run network partition test that kills connections during function-call frames and validate no duplicate tool invocations
rollout_plan: Merge runtime PR behind feature flag
Internal canary (dev account) with full logging for 72 hours
Hosted API canary at 1% traffic for 48 hours, monitor metrics: resume_success_rate, duplicate_tool_calls, resume_latency
If metrics stable, increase to 25% for one week; then 100%
For Dedicated: opt-in by config; communicate to customers and provide migration notes
Deprecation: run legacy resume token mapping for 90 days then require client upgrade
